items.title: Τα φώτα που αφήνουμε αναμμένα θα μπορούσαν να απομακρύνουν το σκοτάδι που χρειάζονται τα δάση της Κεράλα. Δείτε πώς να βοηθήσετε
items.titleOriginal: The Lights We Leave On Could Be Taking Away the Darkness Kerala’s Forests Need. Here’s How to Help
items.description: Ένας δρόμος έξω από ένα δάσος παραμένει φωτισμένος μετά τη δύση του ηλίου. Το ίδιο κάνει και ένας κοντινός τόπος λατρείας ή μια συστάδα καταστημάτων όπου συγκεντρώνεται κόσμος. Αυτά τα φώτα βοηθούν τους ανθρώπους να κάνουν τη ζωή τους. Αλλά η λάμψη τους μπορεί να ταξιδέψει πέρα ​​από τα μέρη που προορίζονται να φωτίσουν. Για την άγρια ​​ζωή που ζει στα Δυτικά Γκάτ της Κεράλα, αυτό εγείρει ένα σημαντικό ερώτημα: πόσο καιρό της νύχτας…
items.descriptionOriginal: A road outside a forest stays lit after sunset. So does a nearby place of worship or a cluster of shops where people gather. Those lights help people go about their lives. But their glow can travel beyond the places they are meant to illuminate. For wildlife living in Kerala's Western Ghats, that raises an important question: how much of the night inside protected forests is still naturally dark? A team of four researchers has begun answering it. Their study, published in Biological Conservation in October 2026, mapped artificial light in and around 21 protected areas in Kerala and examined the roads, buildings and other human activities associated with it. Their findings reveal a conservation concern that is easy to overlook: even where forests have protected boundaries, light from surrounding areas can still reach them. What's causing the forests to light up? Using satellite data from 2024, researchers S. Haripriya, M.S. Arjun, S. Gopakumar and Vijayan Divya measured night-time light across national parks and wildlife sanctuaries. They then compared those measurements with maps showing nearby roads, places of worship, buildings and centres of human activity. The difference between forests was striking. Periyar Tiger Reserve's western division recorded the highest average and peak levels of satellite-measured light among the 21 areas, with a mean radiance of 0.369 and a maximum of 24.0. Kerala's protected areas include tropical evergreen forests, semi-evergreen forests, shola-grassland ecosystems and riverine habitats. Photograph: (Tiger Safari Tours India) Within protected areas, the strongest statistical link was with the density of places of worship. In the surrounding landscape, road networks and places where people gather or work were more important predictors. That distinction matters. Light affecting a forest may be associated with several kinds of human activity, and managing it requires knowing where to look. But light does not always arrive as a visible beam. It can scatter through the atmosphere and brighten the night sky over places some distance away. Researchers call this skyglow . The team examined areas extending up to 30 km beyond forest boundaries. Their modelling suggested that the wider surrounding landscape, particularly the 10–30 km zone, could contribute substantially to skyglow. This means lighting decisions made several kilometres away may influence how dark a protected forest remains at night. Why does darkness matter to wildlife? The Western Ghats are home to many species found nowhere else, including animals active after dark. Natural cycles of light and darkness help wildlife navigate, find food and follow daily rhythms. Research elsewhere has shown that artificial lighting can alter animal behaviour. However, the Kerala study did not directly observe animals or measure how they were affected. That distinction is important. The researchers have identified where artificial light is present and which features of the surrounding landscape are associated with it. Understanding what those light levels mean for different species will require further research. Lead author S. Haripriya has also expressed an interest in investigating these ecological effects in future. Could simple lighting changes help protect these forests? For forest departments and local authorities, the study offers something immediately useful: a way to identify areas where lighting deserves closer attention. A brightly lit road near a forest edge could be assessed for lamps that shine upwards or sideways. Places of worship and tourism facilities could review whether lights need to remain on at full strength throughout the night. Shielded fixtures, lower-intensity lighting and switching off unnecessary lights during periods of low activity are among the options worth considering, while keeping public safety in mind. Periyar Tiger Reserve's western division recorded the highest average and peak levels of satellite-measured light among the 21 areas, with a mean radiance of 0.369 and a maximum of 24.0. Photograph: (Deccan Herald) These are possible next steps rather than changes already implemented because of the study. The findings could, however, help forest officials, local communities and those responsible for public lighting decide where action would be most useful. For years, protecting forests has meant paying attention to what happens within their boundaries. This research offers a reason to look beyond those boundaries, too. And sometimes, protecting a forest's natural environment may begin with something as simple as reconsidering where, when and how we use light. Sources: 'Spatial assessment of artificial light at night in and around protected areas of the Kerala Western Ghats' : By S. Haripriya, M.S. Arjun, S. Gopakumar and Vijayan Divya 'From illumination expansion to ecological response: artificial light at night and detectability of forest vegetation responses across India' : By Dibyendu Dutta, Published on 31 October 2026 'New study examines effect of artificial light at night in protected areas' : By Arathi Menon, Published on 5 November 2026

A nearly invisible layer of magnetic material can overwhelm scientific measurements, producing signals more than 100 times stronger than those of the material researchers are trying to study. items.title: Μελέτη διαπιστώνει ότι ορισμένες αλλαγές στο γονίδιο BRCA2 ενέχουν χαμηλότερο κίνδυνο καρκίνου του μαστού
items.titleOriginal: Study finds some BRCA2 gene changes carry lower breast cancer risk
items.description: Οι ερευνητές της Mayo Clinic, σε μια μελέτη που δημοσιεύτηκε στο Nature Communications, εντόπισαν μια ομάδα παραλλαγών γονιδίου BRCA2 που σχετίζονται με μέτριο κίνδυνο καρκίνου του μαστού, ένα εύρημα που θα μπορούσε να βοηθήσει τις ομάδες υγειονομικής περίθαλψης να αξιολογήσουν καλύτερα τον κίνδυνο καρκίνου ενός ατόμου και να εξατομικεύσουν τη φροντίδα.
items.descriptionOriginal: Mayo Clinic researchers, in a study published in Nature Communications, have identified a group of BRCA2 gene variants associated with a moderate risk of breast cancer, a finding that could help health care teams better assess a person's cancer risk and personalize care.

items.title: «Επιστροφή» λύκων σε Ταΰγετο και Πάρνωνα – Πώς μπορούν να προστατεύσουν οι κτηνοτρόφοι τα κοπάδια τους
items.titleOriginal: «Επιστροφή» λύκων σε Ταΰγετο και Πάρνωνα – Πώς μπορούν να προστατεύσουν οι κτηνοτρόφοι τα κοπάδια τους

Με αφορμή και τον εντοπισμό νεκρής μιας νεαρής λύκαινας την περασμένη Δευτέρα 16/11 500 μέτρα έξω από το χωριό της Αλαγονίας του Ταϋγέτου, ο επιστημονικός συνεργάτης…
items.descriptionOriginal: Στήριξη για τους κτηνοτρόφους του Ταϋγέτου, ώστε να μπορούν να προστατεύσουν τα κοπάδια τους από επιθέσεις λύκων, ζήτησε ο δασολόγος Αλέξης Γιαννακόπουλος, μιλώντας στην εκπομπή «Πρωινό στον Αέρα» στο ραδιόφωνο της ΕΡΤ Καλαμάτας. Με αφορμή και τον εντοπισμό νεκρής μιας νεαρής λύκαινας την περασμένη Δευτέρα 16/11 500 μέτρα έξω από το χωριό της Αλαγονίας του Ταϋγέτου, ο επιστημονικός συνεργάτης της περιβαλλοντικής οργάνωσης «Καλλιστώ» και μέλος ΕΔΙΠ του Πανεπιστημίου Θεσσαλίας χαρακτήρισε εύλογη την ανησυχία των κατοίκων σε μια περιοχή όπου ο λύκος είχε να εμφανιστεί για δεκαετίες. Οι μαρτυρίες για τις επιθέσεις στα κοπάδια Μιλώντας στην εκπομπή «Περίμετρος» της ΕΡΤ3, ο πρόεδρος της Τ.Κ. Αλαγονίας του Δήμου Καλαμάτας, Γιώργος Καζάκος, ο οποίος εντόπισε το νεκρό ζώο, περιέγραψε παράλληλα και τ ην επίθεση λύκων το 2024 σε κοπάδι με 50 κατσίκια στον Ταΰγετο, ενώ όπως είπε και κτηνοτρόφοι από την πλευρά της Λακωνίας έχουν χάσει τουλάχιστον 20 μοσχάρια αλλά και δεκάδες πρόβατα τα τελευταία δυο χρόνια στον Ταΰγετο. «Έχει βιαστεί το οικοσύστημα» , είπε χαρακτηριστικά ο Γιώργος Καζάκος, μιλώντας ευρύτερα για την άγρια ζωή στον Ταΰγετο. Κατά την εκτίμησή του, τα τελευταία χρόνια αυξήθηκαν ραγδαία στην περιοχή τόσο τα τσακάλια όσο και οι αγριόχοιροι. Η επιστροφή των λύκων στον Ταΰγετο Το 2024 η «Καλλιστώ» κατέγραψε στον Ταΰγετο αγέλη εννέα λύκων, επιβεβαιώνοντας την επανεμφάνιση του είδους στην περιοχή έπειτα από σχεδόν έναν αιώνα. Ο κ. Γιαννακόπουλος απέδωσε την επιστροφή στη φυσική εξάπλωση του είδους. Όπως είπε, λύκοι βρίσκονταν ήδη στα Γεράνεια Όρη και σταδιακά πέρασαν στην Πελοπόννησο. Για να εκτιμηθεί πόσοι λύκοι κινούνται σήμερα στον Ταΰγετο, ο δασολόγος είπε ότι χρειάζεται νέα συστηματική παρακολούθηση. Ανέφερε τις κάμερες πεδίου και την ανάλυση DNA από βιολογικό υλικό, όπως τα περιττώματα, ώστε οι ερευνητές να μπορούν να ξεχωρίσουν πόσα διαφορετικά ζώα πέρασαν από την περιοχή. Ο ίδιος συνέδεσε την εξάπλωση των μεγάλων σαρκοφάγων και με την εγκατάλειψη της υπαίθρου. Αναφέρθηκε στα κοπάδια που λιγοστεύουν στον Ταΰγετο και υπογράμμισε ότι η στήριξη των ανθρώπων που εξακολουθούν να ζουν και να εργάζονται στο βουνό μπορεί να συμβάλει στη συνύπαρξη με την άγρια πανίδα. Βίντεο από τους Αγριάνους στον Πάρνωνα Το πρωί της Τρίτης 17 Νοεμβρίου, γύρω στις 11.30, τρεις κυνηγοί βιντεοσκόπησαν λίγο έξω από τους Αγριάνους Λακωνίας, ένα ζώο που αναγνώρισαν ως λύκο. Στα πλάνα που δημοσίευσε το iHunt.gr, το ζώο τρέχει στον δρόμο μπροστά από το αυτοκίνητό τους και στη συνέχεια χάνεται στα δέντρα. Η καταγραφή ενισχύει τις ενδείξεις για παρουσία λύκου και στον Πάρνωνα που μέχρι στιγμής υπήρχαν μόνο ως μαρτυρίες. Ενημέρωση στα χωριά του Ταϋγέτου για τα μέτρα πρόληψης «Η πρόληψη είναι το βασικό» , ανέφερε ο κ. Γιαννακόπουλος. Εξήγησε ότι τα απορρίμματα και τα ζωικά υποπροϊόντα που πετιούνται κοντά στα χωριά προσελκύουν άγρια ζώα. Ζήτησε επίσης να αποφεύγεται η σίτισή τους, καθώς η εύκολη πρόσβαση σε τροφή κοντά στους οικισμούς τα εξοικειώνει με την ανθρώπινη παρουσία. Για την προστασία των κοπαδιών πρότεινε εκπαιδευμένους σκύλους φύλαξης, ηλεκτροφόρες περιφράξεις και ειδικές φωτεινές συσκευές αποτροπής. Ζήτησε ακόμη βελτίωση του κανονισμού του ΕΛΓΑ για τις ζημιές στην κτηνοτροφία και στήριξη των παραγωγών ώστε να μπορούν να εφαρμόσουν τα μέτρα. «Πρέπει να βοηθήσουμε τους κτηνοτρόφους των χωριών του Ταϋγέτου», τόνισε. Ο κ. Γιαννακόπουλος ανέφερε πάντως ότι σχεδιάζεται ενημέρωση το επόμενο χρονικό διάστημα για τους κατοίκους της περιοχής. Για τους κατοίκους των ορεινών χωριών, που δεν είναι εξοικειωμένοι με την παρουσία λύκων, η επίσκεψη ειδικών είναι αναγκαία ώστε να γνωρίζουν πώς να αντιδρούν αν συναντήσουν λύκο. Οι κτηνοτρόφοι θα μπορέσουν επίσης να δουν στην πράξη πώς να προστατεύουν τα κοπάδια τους, περιορίζοντας παράλληλα τον κίνδυνο να τραυματιστούν ή να θανατωθούν άγρια ζώα. Αναλυτικά όσα είπε ο Αλέξης Γιαννακόπουλος στο ραδιόφωνο της ΕΡΤ Καλαμάτας : www.ertnews.gr

items.descriptionOriginal: Η EPOPSIS ΑΜΚΕ Πολιτισμού και το Μεταπτυχιακό Πρόγραμμα Σπουδών « Δημιουργική Γραφή » του Πανεπιστημίου Δυτικής Μακεδονίας , υπό την αιγίδα και με την υποστήριξη του Δήμου Θεσσαλονίκης και της Εταιρίας Λογοτεχνών Θεσσαλονίκης , συνδιοργανώνουν το 2ο International Performance Poetry Biennial Symposium-Festival (PerPoSF #2) . Το Συμπόσιο-Φεστιβάλ ανοίγει τις πύλες του στην πόλη της Θεσσαλονίκης , 4-6 Δεκεμβρίου 2026 . Το PerPoSF #2 έρχεται με τίτλο θεματικής INTRA // BLANC, φωτίζοντας την επιτελεστική ποίηση ως μεταιχμιακή τέχνη, ως αισθητικό πεδίο μετάβασης, ανταλλαγής ενέργειας και έντασης ανάμεσα στη φωνή και τη γραφή, το σώμα και τον λόγο, το υλικό και το άυλο, το παρόν και τη μνήμη, το παροδικό και το τεκμηριωμένο, τον/την δημιουργό και το κοινό, ποικίλες καλλιτεχνικές πρακτικές και νέες τεχνολογίες, μορφές παρουσίας που συνθέτουν το ποιητικό συμβάν ως τέτοιο. Η επιτελεστική ποίηση, καθώς εκδιπλώνεται, παράγει τον ενδιάμεσο χώρο ως δυναμικό γίγνεσθαι σχέσεων και μορφών, εντός μια διαλογικής χωρικότητας και χρονικότητας, αποκαλύπτοντας μια ποιητική του παρόντος, ανοιχτή στη ρήξη, το ενδεχόμενο και την πράξη που μεταμορφώνει. Στο φετινό Συμπόσιο-Φεστιβάλ συμμετέχουν οι προσκεκλημένοι ποιητές/τριες, εισηγητές/τριες, καλλιτέχνες/ιδες και ερευνητές/τριες (με αλφαβητική σειρά): Claus Ankersen (Δανία), Jaan “Luulur” Malin (Εσθονία), Philip Meersman (Βέλγιο), Cia Rinne (Σουηδία), και από την Ελλάδα: Post Fluxus Brothers, Michelle Houwers, Amelia Amlet Medusa, Κωνσταντίνος Αθυρίδης, Βίλη Βάρσου, Γεωργία Βεληβασάκη, Μανώλης Βραχνάκης, Μάρω Γαλάνη, Κατερίνα Ηλιοπούλου, Ζαχαρίας Κατσακός, Γιάννης Μήτρου, Δημήτρης Μπάκας & Νάντια Φιόρου, Μανώλης Νανούρης, Δημήτριος Π. Νάσκος και Ιωάννα Σκαντζέλη. Με αφορμή το ανοιχτό κάλεσμα συμμετέχουν από χώρες του εξωτερικού: Peter Abajkovics (Ουγγαρία), Anastasia Gkitsi/Janni Kolotouros (Γερμανία), Manuela Pellegrino (Κάτω Ιταλία), Pamela Petali & Rakela Hoxka (Αλβανία), Peter Sragher (Ρουμανία), Annegret Suaudeau (Ολλανδία) & Claudia Tesorino (Γερμανία), Emre Varışlı (Τουρκία), Jaan “Luulur” Malin (Εσθονία), Margaret Wesseling (ΗΠΑ), και από την Ελλάδα: Αλέξανδρος Αθανασίου, Ευαγγελία Αραβανή & Μαρία Δασκολιά, Χριστίνα Γεωργιάδου, Βίκη Γκέκινα, Νικόλας Γραίκος, Γαλήνη Ηλιάσκου, Έλενα Π. Καρίκη, Μαρία-Βασιλική Κενανίδου & Εκάβη Whitlock Blundell, Μάρτζυ Κοντέσσα, Χρήστος Κρανιώτης, Πατρίτσια Λάζου, Γιάννης Μαρκάκης, Διονύσης Μαρούλης, Χρυσάνθη Μιχλίζογλου, Πάνος Μπόρας, Άννα Νικολαΐδη, Αριστέα Παπαδοπούλου, Ιωάννης Α. Παπαδόπουλος, Γιούλη Παππού, Βάσια Πασπάλη & Αγγελική Χατζή, Μαρίνα Προβατίδου, Ελισάβετ Πολίτη, Παναγιώτης Σδούκος, Ηλίας Σταυριανός, Όλγα Στεργιοπούλου, Γαρουφαλιά Στέτου, Μαρία Τοπαλίδου και Μαρία Χαρέλα. Poetry Slam Lineup: Athan von Athens, Marialena, Danove, blackberry, Irene, Foivos Zantes, AFK, Ο.Γ.Θ., siev, Cordelia Shibari (συνδιοργάνωση PerPoSF & Poetry Slam GR/Makis Moulos). Μια τριήμερη γιορτή της ποίησης πέρα από τη σελίδα, με δημιουργική ανταλλαγή έργων, απόψεων και ιδεών, με ζωντανές performances, spoken word & slam εκδηλώσεις, ομιλίες/διαλέξεις, συζητήσεις, έργα installed poetry, προβολές video, film & visual/digital poetry, open classes, masterclasses, εργαστήρια επιτελεστικής ποίησης και special events. Εγγραφές: Αποθήκη Δ, ημέρες του Συμποσίου-Φεστιβάλ. Κόστος Συμμετοχής: 30 ευρώ/τριήμερο ή 15 ευρώ/ημέρα. Φοιτητές/φοιτήτριες: Έκπτωση 20%, με την επίδειξη φοιτητικής κάρτας. Άνεργοι/ες: Έκπτωση 20% με την επίδειξη κάρτας ανεργίας. Άτομα με αναπηρία (ΑμεΑ): Δωρεάν είσοδος. www.ertnews.gr

The treatment uses mRNA technology similar to that developed for use in COVID-19 vaccines.

items.descriptionOriginal: Δύο υπερτυχερούς από την Ελλάδα ανέδειξε η κλήρωση του Eurojackpot την Τρίτη (17 Νοεμβρίου), με ένα δελτίο που συμπληρώθηκε στα Τρίκαλα, κόστους 15 ευρώ να τινάζει την μπάνκα στον αέρα, κερδίζοντας 38,3 εκατομμύρια ευρώ. Συγκεκριμένα, στην πρώτη κατηγορία κερδών, όπου απαιτούνταν 5+2 σωστές προβλέψεις, υπήρξαν δύο νικητές, ο ένας από την Ελλάδα. Το δελτίο που έκανε τον κάτοχό του πλουσιότερο κατά 38 εκατομμύρια ευρώ μετά την κλήρωση του Eurojackpot το βράδυ της Τρίτης, συμπληρώθηκε σε πρακτορείο της allwyn στη Θεσσαλία. Όπως ανακοινώθηκε από την εταιρεία, το δελτίο με τις 5+2 επιτυχίες για τα 38.370.583,30 ευρώ – το ένα από τα δύο που κέρδισαν σε όλη την Ευρώπη – συμπληρώθηκε σε πρακτορείο στα Τρίκαλα. Σε δηλώσεις του το πρωί της Τετάρτης στη Λέσχη 97,6, ο ιδιοκτήτης του πρακτορείου στα Τρίκαλα, Κώστας Γεωργίου αποκάλυψε ότι πρόκειται για ένα απλό δελτίο, το κόστος του οποίου δεν ξεπερνούσε τα 15 ευρώ! Οι πέντε αριθμοί που κληρώθηκαν ήταν οι 1, 5, 7, 15 και 19, ενώ οι δύο αριθμοί Euro ήταν οι 1 και 11. Εκτός από τον μεγάλο τυχερό, στην Ελλάδα καταγράφηκε και μια από τις 12 επιτυχίες στη δεύτερη κατηγορία του Eurojackpot (5+1 επιτυχίες) με τον κάτοχο του δελτίου που συμπληρώθηκε στη Θάσο να κερδίζει 159.172 ευρώ. Σημειώνεται ότι το ποσό που θα μοιρασθούν οι τυχεροί της 1ης κατηγορίας στην επόμενη κλήρωση της προσεχούς Παρασκευής (20/11) είναι €10.000.000. items.descriptionOriginal: A patch of dust near a busy road, smoke rising from an industrial chimney, and waste burning in an open space may all contribute to a city's air pollution. But the sources responsible for poor air quality are not necessarily the same across neighbourhoods. This means that a measure addressing pollution in one part of a city may not be equally effective elsewhere. Understanding what contributes to poor air quality at specific locations is therefore an important part of planning cleaner cities . Ahmedabad is attempting to address this challenge by looking beyond citywide air-quality readings and examining pollution at specific locations. The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC), in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, has identified 10 locations across the city for a real-time air-quality monitoring initiative called SMART-VAYU. Reported by The Times of India (TOI) on September 30, 2026, the project aims to identify local pollution hotspots, trace the sources of emissions and generate data that can help civic authorities plan targeted interventions. Initial monitoring exercises at two locations — Sabarmati Riverfront Sports Complex and Narendra Modi Stadium — have already revealed how pollution sources can differ within the same city. One city, two different pollution profiles The initial findings from Ahmedabad offer an interesting look at how the sources contributing to air pollution can vary from one location to another. In its October 17, 2026 report, TOI detailed the findings from air-quality sampling at the Sabarmati Riverfront Sports Complex and Narendra Modi Stadium. Sampling at the riverfront was conducted between May 4 and May 24, while monitoring at Narendra Modi Stadium took place between June 25 and August 8. At the Sabarmati Riverfront, dust accounted for 36% of the estimated source contribution, compared with 23% at Narendra Modi Stadium. Coal combustion contributed 24% at the riverfront, while its estimated contribution at the stadium was just 1%. The pattern was different at Motera. The combined category of marine emissions and refuse burning accounted for 38% of the estimated pollution sources at Narendra Modi Stadium, compared with 16% at the riverfront. Power plant-related sources contributed another 20% at the stadium. The analysis also examined different types of organic aerosols. Traffic-related organic aerosols contributed 18% at Narendra Modi Stadium and 13% at the riverfront. Solid-fuel combustion-related organic aerosols accounted for 16% at the stadium and 5% at the riverfront. These findings highlight an important aspect of urban air pollution: even within one city, different locations can have different pollution profiles . Understanding these differences can help authorities identify which sources need attention in specific areas, rather than approaching air pollution as a uniform problem across the city. Why Ahmedabad is looking beyond citywide AQI readings Identifying the sources behind air pollution is not always straightforward. Citywide air-quality readings provide information about pollution levels, but understanding what is contributing to poor air quality in a particular neighbourhood requires more detailed monitoring. This is the gap that SMART-VAYU aims to address. The initiative stands for Sensing and Monitoring for Air Quality using Real-time Technology – Vision-based Ahmedabad air analysis for Urban Management. The project involves three broad components: mapping existing pollution sources, establishing a hyperlocal monitoring network and developing a decision-support system for urban air-quality management. For civic authorities, this distinction could help connect monitoring with specific pollution-control measures. Photograph: (Ahmedabad Mirror) For this, AMC and IIT Kanpur finalised 10 monitoring locations across Ahmedabad. These include Sabarmati Riverfront Sports Complex, Narendra Modi Stadium, Gujarat Police Academy at Karai, Sanskardham, Veer Savarkar Sports Complex, Pirana AMC community service centre, Rakhial AMC health office, Vatva GIDC's Chandrakala complex, Bopal urban health centre and Thaltej AMC ward office. The selection considered meteorological conditions, particulate matter readings, annual wind patterns, satellite-based aerosol optical depth and estimated PM2.5 concentrations. Practical requirements such as electricity, security, accessibility and airflow were also taken into account. The plan is to deploy five locations with mobile laboratory sampling alongside sensors, while the remaining five will have fixed sensors. The wider project envisages eventually expanding the network to around 400 sensors across Ahmedabad. How the monitoring network will identify pollution sources Unlike conventional monitoring systems that primarily provide broader air-quality readings, these sensors will continuously measure pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, ozone and sulphur dioxide. They will also record meteorological parameters, including temperature and humidity. The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC), in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, has identified 10 locations across the city for a real-time air-quality monitoring. Photograph: (Hindustan Times) An important component is the mobile Real-Time Source Apportionment Laboratory (RTSA), which will help examine the contribution of different pollution sources. Source apportionment is the process of estimating how much different sources contribute to the pollutants present in the air. These could include vehicular emissions, industrial activity, road dust, construction and waste burning. By examining these contributions, the initiative aims to generate pollution hotspot maps, forecasts and alerts that can help authorities identify locations requiring attention. From identifying pollution to planning targeted action Ahmedabad already has an air-quality monitoring network under the Centre's System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research (SAFAR) programme. Its monitoring stations provide city-level air-quality information and forecasts. SMART-VAYU seeks to add another layer of information by examining pollution sources at specific locations. For civic authorities, this distinction could help connect monitoring with specific pollution-control measures. For instance, identifying road dust as a major contributor could inform dust-control and road-cleaning measures. Similarly, evidence of industrial emissions or waste burning could help direct inspections and enforcement. The effectiveness of the initiative will depend on how consistently the monitoring network operates, whether its findings translate into enforceable measures and how improvements in air quality are tracked over time. Ultimately, Ahmedabad's initiative highlights why tackling urban air pollution requires more than understanding how polluted a city is. It also requires knowing what is polluting different parts of it. Because when pollution sources vary from one neighbourhood to another, the solutions must account for those differences too. Sources: 'Ahmedabad: SMART-VAYU to zoom in on air pollution hotspots' : By Kapil Dave, Published on 30 September 2026 'Ahmedabad maps pollution hotspots ahead of 2030 Commonwealth Games' : By Meghdoot Sharon, Published on 17 October 2026 'IIT-K Ahmedabad Gets Real-Time Pollution Tracking Activity' : By Kotak School of Sustainability - IIT Kanpur

items.descriptionOriginal: A flapping-wing robot weighing 1.29 grams (0.045 ounces) has hovered, tracked trajectories, and flown through a cluttered artificial garden using onboard sensing. The insect-scale micro aerial vehicle (IMAV) achieved centimeter-level accuracy, according to a study in Science Robotics from Yi-Hsuan Hsiao and colleagues. In flights guided by a human operator, the robot made multiple 15- to 30-second trips, dodged obstacles, and eventually landed on a sunflower in a mock pollination maneuver. Balancing mass and computation Fully sensor-guided flight at this scale is a balancing act. It requires trading off sensor mass, computation cost, and measurement drift during real-time flight. Aerial insects can navigate dense vegetation with ease, while similarly sized robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation, the authors note. That limits them to motion-capture environments and restricts tasks such as search and rescue or precision agriculture. The team’s framework combines an onboard inertial measurement unit (IMU), a time-of-flight sensor, an optical flow sensor, and a dual-core microcontroller unit (MCU). An IMU measures acceleration and rotation, a time-of-flight sensor estimates height by timing reflected light, and an optical flow sensor tracks motion across the ground. Its estimator and controller run on a single MCU core, leaving room for future communication, image processing, and motion planning. The estimator fuses sensor readings into a position and orientation estimate that the controller uses to steer. Human commands, onboard control The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional accuracy, the preprint says. In a 30-second flight outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. The sunflower served as a mock pollination target, a nod to proposed uses of robotic insects in agriculture. The researchers also built a hierarchical controller that lets a human operator send high-level commands to direct the robot’s motion. The robot still relies on a human for high-level direction, and the authors say onboard planning and power autonomy remain areas to explore. The authors wrote that this level of sensing and computational autonomy is “a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community.” The paper, “Controlled Flight of an Insect-Scale Flapping-Wing Robot via Integrated Onboard Sensing and Computation,” is by Hsiao, Jonathan P. How, Elizabeth Farrell Helbling, YuFeng Chen and colleagues. A growing microrobot field Insect-scale flapping-wing robots have advanced quickly. MIT researchers earlier reported robotic insects that hovered for 1,000 seconds and flipped twice in the air, and Harvard’s RoboBee gained insect-inspired landing gear. Small size makes tiny flyers sensitive to air effects, such as the ground effect near surfaces that complicates landing, as Harvard researchers have noted. MIT’s earlier insect-style microrobot performed somersaults and rapid navigation after gains in speed, acceleration, and hardware durability. Hovering and trajectory tracking, rather than only brief hops, are the baseline skills any free-flying microrobot needs before it can attempt tasks outdoors. Onboard sensing is a key step toward taking such robots out of motion-capture rooms and toward uses such as search and rescue and precision agriculture.

items.descriptionOriginal: Η Ένωση Ασθενών Ελλάδας παρουσίασε στις 31 Οκτωβρίου 2026 το patientsforum.gr, τη νέα ψηφιακή Πλατφόρμα Κοινότητας Συλλόγων Ασθενών, σε εκδήλωση που συνδυάστηκε με σύντομο εκπαιδευτικό εργαστήριο στο ξενοδοχείο Divani Caravel Hotel στην Αθήνα. Η πρωτοβουλία φιλοδοξεί να ενισχύσει τη συστηματική καταγραφή των προβλημάτων που αντιμετωπίζουν οι ασθενείς μέσω των εκπροσώπων τους και ν α αναδείξει τη συλλογική εμπειρία των οργανώσεών τους ως πολύτιμη πηγή τεκμηρίωσης για τον δημόσιο διάλογο και την πολιτική υγείας. Ζητήματα όπως χρόνοι αναμονής, εμπόδια στην πρόσβαση, ελλείψεις προσωπικού και ιατρικών ειδικοτήτων, γεωγραφικές ανισότητες, οικονομική επιβάρυνση και δυσκολίες στον συντονισμό των υπηρεσιών υγείας και περίθαλψης αποτελούν καθημερινές προκλήσεις για τους ασθενείς. Μέσα από το patientsforum.gr , οι οργανώσεις τους αποκτούν ένα κοινό ψηφιακό χώρο για να αποτυπώνουν αυτά τα ζητήματα , να αναγνωρίζουν κοινά προβλήματα και να ανταλλάσσουν εμπειρίες, προτάσεις και καλές πρακτικές. Στόχος είναι οι μεμονωμένες εμπειρίες των ασθενών να συμβάλλουν στη συστηματική αποτύπωση των αναγκών τους και στη διαμόρφωση τεκμηριωμένων παρεμβάσεων και προτάσεων πολιτικής υγείας. Η πλατφόρμα σχεδιάστηκε με τη συμβολή και ανατροφοδότηση των ίδιων των οργανώσεων ασθενών. Συναντήσεις διαλόγου και ομάδες εστίασης σε διαφορετικές περιοχές της χώρας αλλά και διαδικτυακά, ανέδειξαν ανάγκες και προτεραιότητες που αξιοποιήθηκαν για τη διαμόρφωση της δομής και των βασικών λειτουργιών της. Παρουσίαση και πρακτική εξοικείωση με την πλατφόρμα Την εκδήλωση άνοιξε η κυρία Μέμη Τσεκούρα, Πρόεδρος της Ένωσης Ασθενών Ελλάδας, καλωσορίζοντας τους συμμετέχοντες. Στη συνέχεια, η κυρία Ελένη Καρακίτσιου, Programme Officer του Ιδρύματος Μποδοσάκη, παρουσίασε συνοπτικά το πρόγραμμα PLATO, στο πλαίσιο του οποίου υλοποιείται το έργο, υπογραμμίζοντας τη σημασία της πρωτοβουλίας για την ενίσχυση της συμμετοχής και του διαλόγου. Η κυρία Κατερίνα Κουτσογιάννη , Α’ Αντιπρόεδρος της Ένωσης Ασθενών Ελλάδας, αναφέρθηκε στη σημασία της μετατροπής της επιμέρους εμπειρίας σε συλλογική γνώση. Η κυρία Μαρία Βορεάκου , Voreakou IT Consulting, παρουσίασε το περιβάλλον και τις βασικές λειτουργίες του patientsforum.gr, καθοδηγώντας τους συμμετέχοντες σε σύντομη πρακτική εκπαίδευση. Η συνάντηση ολοκληρώθηκε με συζήτηση για τα επόμενα βήματα, με τη συμμετοχή της κυρίας Ρενάτας Βαλσαμή , Scientific Documentation & Health Policy Manager της Ένωσης Ασθενών Ελλάδας, καθώς και με ερωτήσεις και παρατηρήσεις από τους συμμετέχοντες. Τι προσφέρει το patientsforum.gr Μέσω της πλατφόρμας, οι οργανώσεις ασθενών μπορούν να καταγράφουν ζητήματα και εμπειρίες από το σύστημα υγείας, να παρακολουθούν την εξέλιξή τους και να ανταλλάσσουν εμπειρίες, προτάσεις και καλές πρακτικέςς για τη λειτουργία τους. Παράλληλα, φορείς του συστήματος υγείας μπορούν, έχοντας διακριτό ρόλο και διαβαθμισμένη πρόσβαση, να ενημερώνονται για επιλεγμένα ζητήματα και συγκεντρωτικά ευρήματα που αναδεικνύουν οι οργανώσεις. Το patientsforum.gr λειτουργεί ως ψηφιακή κοινότητα με ελεγχόμενη πρόσβαση και διακριτούς ρόλους για τους χρήστες. Δεν αποτελεί δημόσιο χώρο υποβολής καταγγελιών και δεν επιτρέπεται η καταχώριση στοιχείων που θα μπορούσαν να οδηγήσουν στην άμεση ή έμμεση ταυτοποίηση ασθενών. Επόμενος στόχος: Mια ενεργή κοινότητα ασθενών Οι εγγραφές στο patientsforum.gr είναι ήδη ανοιχτές για εκπροσώπους συλλόγων και οργανώσεων ασθενών, καθώς και για εκπροσώπους φορέων του συστήματος υγείας. Η συμμετοχή πραγματοποιείται μέσω αιτήματος εγγραφής και έγκρισης πρόσβασης, σύμφωνα με τον ρόλο κάθε χρήστη. Το επόμενο διάστημα, η Ένωση Ασθενών Ελλάδας θα επικεντρωθεί στην ενεργοποίηση της κοινότητας , στη διεύρυνση της συμμετοχής οργανώσεων και φορέων και στη διάχυση των αποτελεσμάτων που θα προκύψουν από τη λειτουργία της πλατφόρμας. Μπορείτε να δείτε την Πλατφόρμα Κοινότητας Συλλόγων Ασθενών, ΕΔΩ . items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News The Students Giving Tennis a Second Serve Reading Time: 4 minutes A student-run nonprofit born in Flower Mound, Texas, now keeps used tennis balls out of landfills in 16 states. A single tennis ball weighs about two ounces. That is easy to overlook, because nobody throws away just one. Since 2024, BallBack , a student-led nonprofit based in Flower Mound, Texas, has recycled or repurposed more than 160,000 of them. At roughly 58 grams apiece, that is about 9.3 metric tons of rubber and felt, a little over 20,000 pounds. Every one of those balls was headed for the trash. According to RecycleBalls, a tennis ball takes roughly 400 years to break down, slowly shedding microplastics into the surrounding soil. Curbside recycling programs do not accept them. The national picture is larger still. The United States discards an estimated 125 million tennis balls each year, or about 340,000 a day. By comparison, 160,000 balls is less than half a day of the country’s tennis ball waste. What makes BallBack interesting is not only its total so far, but how quickly a model built by high school students is spreading, and how easily it can be copied by anyone with a court, a school, and a car. BallBack began with Prem Kamasani, a varsity tennis player at Flower Mound High School. After practice one evening, he watched his coach getting ready to throw out roughly 400 used balls. He asked whether he could take them instead. “I noticed hundreds of balls going to the trash every week, and no one was doing anything about it,” Kamasani says on BallBack’s website. The balls went home with him. Some went to animal shelters as toys, and others ended up under school chairs. He then began calling local tennis centers to ask whether they had balls to give away as well. Most did. The collection outgrew his family’s garage, then several garages, and teammates joined in. A Lead4Change grant helped turn the school project into a national organization, spreading to over 310 members in 2026. The funding covered prepaid shipping, so courts anywhere in the country could send in their balls at no cost. Partnerships spread across Dallas–Fort Worth, from public facilities such as Kiest and Samuell Grand tennis centers to SMU’s college tennis program and the Flower Mound Animal Shelter. BallBack’s process is deliberately simple. A chapter leader places a free, branded collection bin at a partner facility, such as a tennis center, club, school, or homeowners’ association. Players drop off dead balls after practice instead of tossing them in the trash. Nobody on site has to sort or clean anything. Leaders monitor fill levels and stop by once or twice a month before anything overflows. Recycling bins at Samuell Grand Tennis Center in Dallas, one of BallBack’s partner facilities, let players drop off used tennis balls instead of throwing them away. Photo courtesy of BallBack . Sorting comes next, and it reflects the organization’s priorities. Balls that still bounce are never shredded. They go back into play through youth tennis programs and school teams that cannot afford new equipment, as well as other repurposing partners. Others go to dog shelters as enrichment toys, or to senior living communities, where they serve as walker feet. BallBack boxes only the balls with no play left in them, labels them with prepaid UPS shipping, and sends them to RecycleBalls or the USTA, BallBack’s national recycling partners. There, they separate the rubber and felt and grind them into crumb rubber that becomes new tennis court surfaces, playground padding, and footing for equestrian arenas. Through RecycleBalls and USTA, BallBack’s shipments help feed a North American collection network of roughly 10,000 locations. BallBack now runs with a national team of students recruited from across the country, each responsible for a distinct part of the work. The media team shapes how BallBack tells its story, from pickup-day footage to chapter spotlights. The marketing team carries that story to new schools, players, and facilities. The onboarding team brings each new chapter leader up to speed with step-by-step guides, so a student in Seattle or Fort Lauderdale can complete a first pickup within a week of signing up. Leaders trade questions and progress in a shared online community. This structure lets the network grow without relying on any one person. BallBack now counts 31 student chapter leaders across 16 states, more than 310 members, and over 55 partner facilities. Chapters operate in New York City, Philadelphia, Chicago, Portland, Seattle, Minneapolis, Folsom, and Green Bay, among other cities. In Manhattan, one senior ships roughly 750 balls a month. In Falls Church, Virginia, chapter leader Surya Arivumani has already recycled more than 1,200. BallBack is set up so that taking part does not depend on where you live. High school sophomores, juniors, and rising seniors in any U.S. city without an existing chapter can apply to start one at their local school. The commitment is one or two pickup trips a month, an hour or two each, for at least four months. Costs are close to zero, and leaders unlock $60 in credit after their first shipment. New chapter leaders are accepted every quarter. Tennis facilities near an existing chapter can list themselves as operating partners and receive free bins, pickups, and shipping. Facilities elsewhere can join as affiliate partners and ship their own boxes for free using prepaid FedEx labels. Individuals with a bag of old balls in the garage can also request a free shipping label, pack a box, and drop it off at FedEx. In Dallas–Fort Worth, anyone with 100 or more balls can arrange a free pickup. BallBack’s next milestone is a world record for the most tennis balls recycled in a single week. The plan is a coordinated national recycling week in spring of 2027. Chapter leaders, members, and partner facilities nationwide would collect, sort, and ship tennis balls at the same time. The effort is still being organized, as BallBack has yet to choose an adjudicator to set the rules for counting and verifying the balls. Whatever the final tally, the week is designed to do what no single chapter can: show what happens when hundreds of courts in dozens of cities choose to recycle at once. Long before BallBack, Kamasani’s father sent him to gather old balls from behind their neighborhood courts instead of buying new ones. Today, Kamasani mentors student leaders he’s never met in cities he’s never visited, who are doing the same thing on a national scale. In BallBack’s latest milestone update, he wrote that the 160,000 mark showed what “a bin by the fence and a student with a car” can accomplish. Students interested in starting a chapter, facilities that want to host a bin, and players with balls to donate can find details at ballback.org . The post The Students Giving Tennis a Second Serve appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Japanese Scientists Design a Plant-Based Plastic that can Become Fertilizer Reading Time: 3 minutes Researchers at Chiba University have developed a flexible, plant-based plastic that can be turned into crop fertilizer after use. Plant-based plastic often ends up in the same places as ordinary plastic, from landfills to incinerators. A research team in Japan wants to give it a more useful ending. What if a used plastic film could help grow the next crop? Associate Professor Daisuke Aoki of Chiba University led the study . Colleagues from the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University joined the work. They published their results in the journal Scientific Reports in August 2026. The need for new ideas is growing. Global plastic use reached 460 million metric tons in 2019, according to the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. If current trends continue, it could climb to 1.2 billion metric tons by 2060. Recycling and waste-to-energy plants are struggling to keep pace with this growth. Aoki’s team took a different route by designing a plastic with its end-of-life already planned. The material starts with isosorbide, a nontoxic compound made from glucose. Glucose is a simple sugar that can come from plant starch, such as corn. Chemists link isosorbide units into a clear, hard plastic called poly(isosorbide carbonate). In 2021, Aoki and his students showed that warm ammonia water breaks down this plastic. The process splits it back into isosorbide and urea. Urea is one of the world’s most widely used nitrogen fertilizers. Aoki compared the goal to the Haber-Bosch process, which turned nitrogen from the air into fertilizer a century ago. His team hoped to turn plastic waste into food in a similar way. Their conversion also needed no costly metal catalysts. One problem remained. The original plastic was hard and brittle, stretching only about 4% before it snapped. That limited it to a narrow range of rigid products. Most plastics are softened with additives called plasticizers. Common ones, such as phthalates, do not break down into anything useful. Some also raise health concerns. The Chiba team designed a plasticizer for its plant-based plastic from the same building block. It has an isosorbide core linked to two short triethylene glycol chains, a common industrial chemical. Like the plastic, it breaks apart when treated with ammonia. With the new plasticizer, the material stretched about 45% before breaking, more than ten times as far as before. It also began to soften at about 40 degrees Celsius instead of 161 degrees, a sign of greater flexibility. Unlike a phthalate blend, the new mix stayed clear and uniform at every mixing ratio. The phthalate version turned cloudy, indicating its ingredients had separated. The team also made a longer-chain version of the plasticizer that stretched the plastic even further. It could be made at yields above 80%, versus under 25% for the first version. That makes it more practical to produce at scale. Converting the used plastic is simple. The team heated it in ammonia water at 90 degrees Celsius for 24 hours. The solid plastic dissolved completely into a clear liquid. That liquid held most of the original building blocks. The team recovered about 98% of the isosorbide, 78% of the possible urea, and 90% of the glycol. Some carbon escaped as carbon dioxide, and better conditions could raise the urea yield. Next came the most important test. The researchers used the liquid as fertilizer without any purification. They tried it on a common lab plant and on komatsuna, a leafy green often called Japanese mustard spinach. Over 36 days in a greenhouse, komatsuna grown with the recycled product matched plants fed commercial urea. Both groups grew far better than plants given no nitrogen. In the lab, the product performed at least as well as urea alone. Komatsuna grown with fertilizer from recycled plant-based plastic matched plants fed commercial urea. Photo courtesy of Scientific Reports . The authors are clear about the limits. Their plant-based plastic is not biodegradable, so it only becomes fertilizer after chemical treatment. Its strength is also not yet high enough for demanding uses. Other questions remain open. The team has not yet tested whether the plasticizer leaks out over time. They also have not measured the full energy cost and environmental footprint of the conversion process. Even so, the researchers see clear uses ahead. This plant-based plastic could be used for agricultural mulch films, seedling pots, shopping bags, and packaging. Farms could then turn used films and pots into fertilizer on site. Aoki believes plastics are at a turning point. He hopes people will one day see plastic waste as a valuable resource for growing food rather than trash. If that happens, plant-based plastic could complete a full circle. Plant-based material would return to the soil to feed new plants. The post Japanese Scientists Design a Plant-Based Plastic that can Become Fertilizer appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: “Just eat less.” “Work harder.” “Have some willpower.” We hear it all the time. But if weight loss were that simple, why can keeping it off feel even harder? Because sometimes, your own biology pushes back. After you lose weight, your body can respond with stronger hunger signals and lower energy use. These biological adaptations can favour weight regain. Does that mean weight always comes back? No. It means long-term medical support may need more than a short burst of willpower. And struggling doesn’t mean someone is lazy or lacks discipline. Weight is shaped by biology, behaviour and environment. If you keep struggling, continue with practical nutrition, movement, strength and sleep habits. And if weight repeatedly returns, or the plan feels impossible to sustain, speak to a qualified doctor about long-term weight management and the biological or practical barriers involved. Getting medical support is not failure. Talk to a qualified doctor about your weight management. This is general information, not a diagnosis or medical advice. #CountWhatMatters #WeightRegain #WeightManagement #Biology #HealthJourney [why weight comes back after weight loss, body pushes back after weight loss, hunger signals and weight regain, struggling with weight is not a character flaw, India]

items.descriptionOriginal: Welcome back to our weekly behind-the-scenes glimpse at what’s getting our team talking. Tell us what you’ve been reading at info@reasonstobecheerful.world and we just might feature it here. Get smart Over the last decade, the rise of smartphones across the U.S. has coincided with a significant drop in kids’ performance at school. Now, as the New York Times reports in a story shared by Executive Editor Will Doig, a new study has found that school phone bans are leading to modest improvements. Published this week by the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard, the study included 3.3 million students in third through tenth grade, comparing the math and reading test scores of students at schools with and without strict phone bans. Though the gains seen at the schools with phone bans were modest, they suggest that gradual improvement is underway. Will says: As a parent, there are so many reasons I’m in favor of banning phones at school, academics being just one of them. Still, it’s great to see data showing proof of concept on that aspect. Mapping roots In other phone-related news, there’s now an app that can help you find remarkable old trees. According to a Guardian article shared by Editorial Director Rebecca Worby, Ancient Trees offers a curated map of notable trees. “I thought it was quite a niche, geeky thing,” the app’s creator, Hidde Burgmans, told the Guardian, “but apparently more people are interested in ancient trees than I thought.” Becca says: On the one hand, using an app takes away the serendipity of just happening into a notable tree. On the other hand, I do like the idea of people detouring to see cool trees . What else we’re reading Minnesota announces ‘effective end’ to veteran homelessness, achieving decades-long goal — shared by Contributing Editor Michaela Haas from KSTP Free tool helps young men to take responsibility for sexual harm — shared by Contributing Editor Geetanjali Krishna from Positive News ‘Music is the most powerful way of connecting to what’s happening’: can this album change your mind about the climate crisis? — shared by Michaela Haas from the Guardian In other news… Turns out people love moss! Our Instagram video about how moss is taking over cities has really taken off. To learn more about all the cool things moss can do, read Michaela Haas’s great story. The post What We’re Reading: Phone Bans Are Improving Kids’ Test Scores appeared first on Reasons to be Cheerful .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Mycelium Leather at Mass-Production Scale Moves Closer to Reality Reading Time: 3 minutes Finnish researchers found a way to make mycelium leather at mass-production scale using papermaking methods. Mycelium leather at mass-production scale may be within reach, according to new research from VTT Technical Research Center of Finland. The team made leather-like sheets using a continuous process rather than slow-growing trays. The study appeared in ACS Applied Bio Materials in July 2026. Mycelium is the underground network of fibers below mushroom caps. Researchers see it as a promising animal-free material for bags, shoes, and clothing. The hard part has been making enough of it. Most mycelium materials grow in trays. Fungi spread across the tray until the fibers knit into one solid sheet. That works for small batches but cannot support mycelium leather at mass-production scale. The VTT team took a different path. They grew a fungus called Trichoderma reesei using submerged fermentation. That means the fungus grows in a nutrient-rich liquid inside a bioreactor. A bioreactor is a tank with controlled growing conditions. The result is a wet mycelium pulp. The researchers washed the pulp and mixed it with sorbitol and cellulose. Sorbitol is a sugar-based softener that keeps the sheet from becoming brittle. Cellulose is a plant fiber that adds strength. The formulas used nanofibrillated cellulose, which is cellulose broken into extremely fine fibers. Sorbitol acts as a plasticizer, an additive that makes materials more flexible. Together, they shape how the finished sheet feels and performs. The team then spread the mix into thin sheets and dried them. The result is a nonwoven fabric, meaning the fibers are bonded together rather than woven or knitted. The researchers could handle, cut, and sew it much like a regular textile. Strength matters for any leather substitute. Tests showed tensile strength of 11 to 19 megapascals (MPa), depending on how the mycelium was pretreated. That number measures how much pulling force a material handles before it breaks. The sheets also stretched about 9% to 10% before fracturing. That flexibility matters for products like bags and shoes, which bend and flex every day. Scale was the real test. The team adapted a roller system similar to those used in paper manufacturing. It produced continuous sheets about 8 inches wide and 26 feet long. That is roughly the width of a letter-size page and the length of a large moving truck. The team used a roll-to-roll pilot line and a wet-casting process. Wet casting means spreading liquid pulp into a thin layer that dries into a sheet. It is still a pilot run. But it shows that mycelium leather at mass-production scale can move past small lab samples. Researchers in Finland used liquid fermentation and a roller line to bring mycelium leather at mass-production scale closer to reality. Photo by Cottonbro Studio on Pexels. Using familiar equipment could matter as much as the material itself. Manufacturers might not need to build entirely new production lines from scratch. That could lower the cost and risk of trying a new material. Co-author Manuel Arias-Barrantes said the work solves a major bottleneck in large-scale, affordable production. He noted that scalable options remain limited today. The pulp approach also gives researchers more control over the final material. They can adjust its properties, add color and texture, or layer it onto cotton fabric. The recipe is easy to change, opening the door to different products. The researchers sewed a prototype accessory bag from black-dyed mycelium fabric. It shows the material can take color and hold stitching. That is a practical first step toward real products. Why does this matter for shoppers? Many vegan leathers are made from petroleum-based plastics that are difficult to recycle. Animal leather also has environmental costs, including livestock and chemical processing. Géza Szilvay of VTT said the process uses renewable feedstocks and mild conditions. It involves no livestock and no chemically intensive steps. He believes the concept could become a viable alternative to non-renewable synthetic leathers, and scaling mycelium leather to mass production is central to that goal. Researchers describe the finished fabric as compostable. That could give it an advantage over plastic-based options at the end of a product’s life. It also supports a wider shift toward materials made from renewable sources. See also: Converting Kombucha to Green Textiles for Sustainable Fashion Questions remain. Mycelium materials still need further development to meet the demands of tough, everyday uses. Long-term durability and cost at factory volume will need testing. Mycelium is not the only plant-based option under study. Brands are also exploring leathers made from cactus and pineapple leaves. Several clothing companies already use pineapple leaf material in garments. Still, the study offers a clear path forward. A handbag grown in a tank and dried on a roller line no longer sounds far-fetched. If later tests hold up, mycelium leather at mass-production scale could give brands a renewable option made with familiar equipment. The post Mycelium Leather at Mass-Production Scale Moves Closer to Reality appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.descriptionOriginal: Festive decorations bring colour and warmth to a home, but a little greenery can make the space feel even more inviting. If you want to give your living room, entrance, or balcony a fresh look this festive season, tall indoor plants are a lovely way to do it. They add height, fill empty corners, and bring a natural charm to your decorations. Pair them with earthen pots, warm fairy lights, or a few diyas , and these plants can become part of your festive decor. Here are 10 tall houseplants worth considering. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lazy Gardener (@lazygardener.in) 1. Rubber Plant With its broad, glossy leaves and upright growth, the rubber plant makes a striking addition to any room. Its deep green foliage looks particularly beautiful against light-coloured walls. It prefers bright, indirect light and watering when the top layer of soil dries out. The rubber plant makes a striking addition to any room. Photograph: (Leaf Envy) 2. Bird of Paradise Known for its large, banana-like leaves, the bird of paradise brings a tropical feel indoors. Given enough light and space, it can grow quite tall. Place it near a bright window and water when the soil begins to dry. Known for its large, banana-like leaves, the bird of paradise brings a tropical feel indoors. Photograph: (Plant Drop) 3. Money Tree The money tree is loved for its distinctive braided trunk and clusters of green leaves. Usually associated with prosperity and good fortune, it makes a fitting addition to festive homes. It grows well in bright, indirect light and prefers well-draining soil. The money tree is loved for its distinctive braided trunk and clusters of green leaves. Photograph: (Patch Plants) 4. Areca Palm Its arching, feathery fronds give the areca palm a soft, tropical appearance. It works particularly well in living rooms and near entrances where it has room to spread. Keep it in bright, indirect light and maintain lightly moist soil. Its arching, feathery fronds give the areca palm a soft, tropical appearance. Photograph: (Amazon.in) 5. Monstera The monstera stands out for its large, naturally split leaves. Its dramatic foliage adds character without requiring complicated decoration. It prefers bright, indirect light and moderate watering . Give it a moss pole or support as it grows. The monstera stands out for its large, naturally split leaves. Photograph: (unlimitedgreens) 6. Fiddle Leaf Fig With its oversized, violin-shaped leaves, the fiddle leaf fig makes a beautiful statement plant. It looks especially elegant in a simple ceramic planter. Place it in a bright spot with indirect sunlight and avoid moving it around frequently. With its oversized, violin-shaped leaves, the fiddle-leaf fig makes a beautiful statement plant. Photograph: (Mason Home) 7. Dracaena Dracaena varieties are known for their upright growth and attractive foliage. Some have slender leaves with colourful edges, making them a good choice for narrow corners. They prefer indirect light and need watering only when the soil starts drying out. Dracaena varieties are known for their upright growth and attractive foliage. Photograph: (Thursd) 8. Yucca The yucca's woody stem and pointed leaves give it a distinctive, sculptural appearance. It is a good option for those who prefer plants that need less frequent watering. Keep it near a sunny window and allow the soil to dry between waterings. The yucca's woody stem and pointed leaves give it a distinctive, sculptural appearance. Photograph: (Fourwalls) 9. Elephant Ear As the name suggests, elephant ear plants have enormous, heart-shaped leaves that instantly catch the eye. Their lush foliage brings a tropical touch to indoor spaces. They prefer bright, indirect light, humidity, and consistently moist, well-draining soil. As the name suggests, elephant ear plants have enormous, heart-shaped leaves that instantly catch the eye. Photograph: (Bloomica) 10. Croton If your festive decor needs a burst of colour, the croton is a wonderful choice. Its leaves feature captivating shades of green, yellow, orange, and red. It needs plenty of bright light to maintain its vibrant colours and should be watered when the topsoil begins to dry. If your festive decor needs a burst of colour, the croton is a wonderful choice. Photograph: (Nista) Whether you prefer the deep green leaves of a rubber plant or the colourful foliage of a Croton, these houseplants can give your home a festive makeover that lasts well beyond the celebrations. Choose plants according to the light and space available, dress up their pots, and let the greenery do the rest.

items.description: Αντίγραφο: Για περισσότερες από πέντε δεκαετίες, το έργο τέχνης του βρήκε μια θέση σε εκατομμύρια ινδικά σπίτια, και έγινε οικείο θέαμα από γενιά σε γενιά. Ο καλλιτέχνης S.M. Ο Srinivasan, ο οποίος πέθανε στα 86 του, ήταν γνωστός για τους πίνακές του με θεότητες, ειδικά για τις δύο εμβληματικές απεικονίσεις του Λόρδου Venkateswara, οι οποίες έγιναν ευρέως αναγνωρισμένες μέσω ημερολογίων, αφισών και εκτύπωσης σε κορνίζα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Copy: For over five decades, his artwork found a place in millions of Indian homes, becoming a familiar sight across generations. Artist S.M. Srinivasan, who passed away at 86, was known for his paintings of deities, especially his two iconic depictions of Lord Venkateswara, which became widely recognised through calendars, posters and framed prints. Born in Kovilpatti, Tamil Nadu, Srinivasan studied up to Class 10 before learning the art of painting under renowned artist Kondaiah Raju. In 1970, he got a rare opportunity to observe and paint the idol at the Tirumala temple. He created two versions, one with elaborate ornaments and another without them. Approved by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), his paintings were reproduced as calendars, posters and framed prints. Soon, his artwork became a familiar sight on calendars across India, finding its way into homes, shops and everyday spaces. For generations, these familiar images became part of India’s visual and cultural landscape. While many may not have known the artist behind them, his work remained a part of their everyday lives. #Srinivasan #SMSrinivasan #TirupatiBalaji #IndianArt [S.M. Srinivasan artist, Lord Venkateswara painting artist, Tirupati Balaji calendar image]

items.title: Το «Everybody Wants to Rule the World» δεν μοιάζει καθόλου με το τραγούδι του Don Henley που το ενέπνευσε
items.titleOriginal: ‘Everybody Wants to Rule the World’ sounds nothing like the Don Henley song that inspired it
items.description: Μερικές δεκαετίες είναι απλώς μεγαλύτερες από άλλες, αλλά η δεκαετία του 1980 μπορεί να τις ξεπέρασε όλες, ειδικά όταν πρόκειται για μουσική. Από την άνοδο του χιπ χοπ μέχρι την κυριαρχία του hair metal, η εποχή είναι γεμάτη με ποπ τελειότητα. Τα πρώτα μισά της δεκαετίας ορίστηκαν από τη μαζική εισβολή του «Νέου Κύματος». Τα λαμπρά βρετανικά συγκροτήματα διέσχισαν τον Ατλαντικό εξυπνάδα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Some decades are just bigger than others, but the 1980s might have outdone them all, especially when it comes to music . From the ascendance of hip hop to the dominance of hair metal, the era is filled with pop perfection . The early half of the decade was defined by the massive “New Wave” invasion . Brilliant British bands crossed the Atlantic with clever synthesizers, angular rhythms, and stylish haircuts. Groups like Duran Duran, Depeche Mode, and the Eurythmics totally reshaped the music charts . Among these electronic pioneers stood Tears for Fears. Formed in England by Kent natives Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith, the duo released their critically acclaimed debut album, The Hurting , in 1983. They established themselves as masters of moody, introspective synth-pop, climbing to the Top 5 of the U.K. charts with three singles from the album, including the enduring “Mad World.” When it came time to record their second album, 1985’s Songs from the Big Chair , the pressure on the pair of musicians was immense. Every single track took an agonizingly long time to put together. The band labored over every drumbeat, chord progression, and lyric. Some took an entire year to produce. Just as finishing up the record finally seemed within reach, their record label stepped in with a directive: add a catchy new track to boost crossover appeal in the United States. The surprising spark for what would become one of their most enduring hits came from an unlikely musical source: former Eagles drummer Don Henley. The Don Henley groove that changed everything Scouring American radio for inspiration, Smith and Orzabal analyzed what made U.S. pop hits click. “Driving songs are American,” Smith noted, pointing to the unstoppable momentum of classic stateside road trip anthems. This observation is what led the pair to Don Henley’s massive 1984 hit, “The Boys of Summer.” The track’s infectious, driving rhythm inspired Orzabal to rethink some simple guitar and keyboard riffs he had been messing around with. Like “Boys of Summer,” their song has a “driving with the windows-down” momentum. It also channels Henley’s sarcastic melancholy about the decade. The lyrics in the track evoke the nuclear arms race between the U.S. and the USSR at the time. Originally, the song was titled “Everyone Wants to Go to War.” Orzabal tunes his guitar down, building a shimmering, shuffling groove around a simple chord progression. The song was completed in just over a week , a far cry from the tracks they’d been laboring over for more than a year. Today, we know it as the bright, upbeat masterpiece titled “Everybody Wants to Rule the World.” A record label gamble and enduring legacy Despite the song’s undeniable sunshine feel, the lyrics carry a serious message about power, greed, and political control. This made the band’s American distributor’s enthusiasm for the tune even more surprising. They wanted “Everybody…” to be the lead single in the U.S. Orzabal and Smith immediately objected. They preferred the more synth-focused “Mother’s Talk,” which peaked at #14 in the U.K. The guitar-forward “Everybody…” debuted in March of 1985 in the States. The label’s gamble paid off instantly. The track rocketed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and turned Tears for Fears into global superstars. It didn’t hurt that the pair also had several music videos from the album. It was perfect timing to be added to MTV’s roster. Just one year later, “Everybody…” was selected as the memorable end-credits song for the 1985 film, Real Genius . Decades later, its cultural footprint refuses to fade. The song regularly charts on streaming platforms. It even returned to #1 on Billboard ‘s Alternative Digital Song Sales chart in March 2021 . In June 2026, the song reached #23 on the Streaming Rock Charts and has spent more than 200 non-consecutive weeks on the Global 200 chart . Today it remains an immortal ’80s anthem born from an unlikely cross-Atlantic musical influence. So if you find yourself taking a drive this week, don’t forget to crank up a little Tears for Fears and sing along. After all, “ Nothing ever lasts forever. Everybody wants to rule the world.” The post ‘Everybody Wants to Rule the World’ sounds nothing like the Don Henley song that inspired it appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Η Tesla αποκαλύπτει την πιο προηγμένη πλατφόρμα ισχύος στερεάς κατάστασης στον κόσμο με απόδοση 98,86%
items.titleOriginal: Tesla unveils world’s most advanced solid-state power platform with 98.86% efficiency
items.description: Η Tesla παρουσίασε μια νέα πλατφόρμα ηλεκτρονικών ισχύος που θα μπορούσε να αλλάξει τον τρόπο σύνδεσης μεγάλων ενεργειακών έργων με το ηλεκτρικό δίκτυο. Ονομάζεται Powercore, το σύστημα συνδυάζει πολλές λειτουργίες μετατροπής ισχύος σε μια ενιαία μονάδα μέσης τάσης. Στοχεύει στις αυξανόμενες απαιτήσεις ηλεκτρικής ενέργειας από κέντρα δεδομένων, εγκαταστάσεις αποθήκευσης μπαταριών και ηλιακή ενέργεια σε κλίμακα χρησιμότητας…
items.descriptionOriginal: Tesla has unveiled a new power electronics platform that could change how large energy projects connect to the electrical grid. Called Powercore, the system combines several power conversion functions into a single medium-voltage unit. It targets growing electricity demands from data centers, battery storage facilities, and utility-scale solar installations. The platform aims to reduce conversion losses while simplifying electrical infrastructure. Tesla plans to manufacture Powercore in the United States, with its first units expected to enter operation in 2027. A new approach to power conversion Powercore combines the functions of a transformer, inverter, and circuit breaker inside one enclosure. It converts electricity between medium-voltage alternating current (AC) and low-voltage direct current (DC). Conventional installations typically require separate equipment to handle these tasks. Tesla claims the platform achieves peak efficiency of 98.86 percent. It can deliver up to 9 megavolt-amperes (MVA), equivalent to 7.4 megawatts continuously. Its grid-forming configuration can also reach 10 MVA. Introducing Powercore Solid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure 7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak power Made in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf — Tesla Megapack (@Tesla_Megapack) November 17, 2026 The system supports AC voltages between 10 and 34.5 kilovolts. Its DC operating range extends from 800 to 2,000 volts. Tesla has also integrated a solid-state circuit breaker that reportedly clears electrical faults up to 1,000 times faster than conventional breakers. Faster fault clearing can limit electrical damage and improve equipment protection. Powercore also eliminates the flammable insulating oil used in conventional transformers. Its modular design allows technicians to service individual components without replacing the entire unit. Tesla plans to offer warranties of up to 25 years. The company also promises system availability guarantees of at least 99.9 percent. Targeting next-generation data centers Data centers represent one of the platform’s biggest potential applications. Their growing computing demands require increasingly complex power infrastructure. Most facilities currently receive electricity at 415 to 480 volts AC before converting it for different systems. The industry is moving toward 800-volt DC architectures. Powercore can convert medium-voltage electricity directly into 800-volt DC. That eliminates intermediate conversion stages and could reduce the equipment needed inside large facilities. Tesla says lower conversion losses could allow operators to run more GPUs using the same available grid connection. Built-in redundancy also gives Powercore a claimed product-level availability of up to 99.7 percent. Tesla is working with Nvidia on engineering efforts to support 800-volt DC power architectures in future data centers. Megapack battery systems can also connect directly to the DC bus. They provide backup power and help manage fluctuations in electricity demand. Bringing solar and storage together Powercore also addresses challenges facing utility-scale solar developers. Transformer supply shortages can delay new installations, while inverter failures contribute to lost generation. Tesla’s platform converts electricity from solar arrays directly into medium-voltage AC. It supports existing 1,500-volt DC solar installations and emerging 2,000-volt systems. Its modular design also allows technicians to service components without replacing entire units. Battery storage projects could benefit from a similar change. Conventional Megapack installations use two conversion stages to move electricity between batteries and the grid. Powercore reduces that process to a single stage, potentially improving efficiency and energy output. Tesla estimates that a 100-megawatt data center could run on 500 megawatts of solar capacity paired with 1.7 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. The configuration would allow the facility to draw power from solar and storage systems through an 800-volt DC architecture. Powercore will be manufactured in the United States, although Tesla has not provided a specific production start date. The company currently reports 140 GWh of annual Megapack manufacturing capacity. Of that total, 90 GWh comes from facilities across California, Texas, and Nevada.

Ο στρατηγός των Rookie Raiders, Fernando Mendoza, πέτυχε το πρώτο του touchdown NFL σε έναν αγώνα εναντίον των Seattle Seahawks στις 15 Νοεμβρίου 2026. Αλλά αντί να πηδήξει από τις θέσεις του σταδίου τους για να επευφημήσει, ο R.…
items.descriptionOriginal: An unexpectedly sweet gesture from thousands of Las Vegas Raiders fans has brought football lovers around the country together, even from rival teams. Rookie Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza landed his first NFL touchdown in a match-up against the Seattle Seahawks on November 15, 2026. But instead of leaping from their stadium seats to cheer, Raiders fans stayed seated to celebrate the big moment. Why? Because that’s what Mendoza’s parents do for every one of their son’s achievements. View this post on Instagram Mendoza’s mom has multiple sclerosis and uses a wheelchair As a standout college quarterback in 2025, Mendoza became the first Heisman Trophy winner (an annual award recognizing the best college football player in the nation) from Indiana University. He was also the top NFL draft pick for the 2026 season. And in the background of all of those wins sat his mom, Elsa, who lives with multiple sclerosis, and his dad, Fernando Sr., who always sits in solidarity with her. Elsa Mendoza was diagnosed with MS in 2008 , when Fernando was just a young child. The disease has since progressed to the point where she uses a wheelchair for mobility. Fernando Sr. chooses to sit with his wife while others rise and cheer at games, keenly aware of how much it limits her view when everyone around her is standing. Members of Raiders Nation take note and rally others to stay seated Many fans who entered Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas for the game against the Seahawks were greeted by a man holding a sign asking people to stay seated during Mendoza’s first touchdown, scored in honor of his mom. Raider Nation, hear me out: when Mendoza scores his first TD at Allegiant let’s all stay seated and celebrate like his dad. We can raise a ton of awareness for MS research and it’ll be an all-timer kind of gesture from fan base to player. https://t.co/CiiQyWutNa — Tom Joanides (@TJoanides) July 1, 2026 The notice initially went out on social media in July, when Raiders fan Tom Joanides suggested celebrating as the Mendozas do to raise awareness for MS. At that point, the idea didn’t get any traction. “I don’t have a huge account or anything, so I was like yelling into the void,” Joanides told ESPN . But when Joanides repeated the suggestion in the week leading up to Mendoza’s first career start, it took off. Then the idea started spreading around Raider Nation. Listen, everyone going to Allegiant Stadium this Sunday. Stay seated when Fernando scores his first touchdown. Will be an epic gesture from fans to player. Pass it along. — Tom Joanides (@TJoanides) November 11, 2026 Upworthy’s own Tod Perry, a long-time Raiders fan who attended the game, shares how he and his son participated with others in the stands. “I saw a post about sitting for Mendoza’s mom on X, in a post by Mitchell Renz from The Raiders Report on Chat Sports,” Perry says. “It took some real fortitude to remain seated after Fernando ran in the touchdown, because it was so exciting. It was the moment the fans have waited a long time for. Every part of me wanted to jump up, but I stayed seated and reminded my 10-year-old son to stay put out of respect for Fernando’s mom.” Mendoza was grateful for the love shown to him and his family When you’re out on the field making big plays, especially in your first NFL game, you’re probably not keenly aware of what’s happening in the crowd. Mendoza didn’t learn about the thousands who sat for his mom until after the game. View this post on Instagram “Wow,” Mendoza responded when a reporter explained what the fans had done. “I was not aware of that, but I’m super grateful to the Silver and Black for doing that. That means a lot to my family and I, and I just can’t thank you guys enough.” Elsa’s MS journey has long overlapped with her son’s football journey and will continue to do so. One of the first things Mendoza did after being drafted was commit $500,000 to launch the Mendoza Family Fund in partnership with the National Multiple Sclerosis Society to support MS research. Even people outside of Raider Nation loved seeing the kind and thoughtful gesture and the gratitude that followed it: “Cheering for him as a Bronco fan and 23 year MS Warrior!! All love for Mendoza!” “This kid has a bright NFL future. He gave my Seahawks some trouble early on today. Can’t help but root for the kid.” “So much respect for Raider fans for doing that for their QB and his Mom. Love this!” “Raiders fans: my respects ” “As a Niner fan I respect the Raider Nation a lot more for this ” “Not a Raiders fan but lots of respect for this.” You don’t have to be a fan of any particular team to appreciate humans collectively paying respect to an extraordinary family in an extraordinary way, especially when that collective kind gesture comes from a notoriously intense fanbase. As Perry pointed out, “It was really touching to see Raider Nation, who sometimes get a bad rap for being a bit too rowdy, hold it together for a player’s mom.” Indeed it was. The post The Raiders’ rookie quarterback scored his first NFL touchdown. Thousands of fans stayed seated to honor his mom. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Οι επιστήμονες πέρασαν 13 χρόνια παρακολουθώντας τζάγκουαρ. Αυτό που είδαν αμφισβήτησε μια μακροχρόνια πεποίθηση.
items.titleOriginal: Scientists spent 13 years watching jaguars. What they saw challenged a long-held belief.
items.description: Οι γάτες έχουν έναν τρόπο να μπλέκουν με τις προσδοκίες μας. Ακόμη και η ταπεινή γάτα του σπιτιού αποδεικνύεται λιγότερο απόμακρη και αντικοινωνική από ό,τι πιστεύαμε παλαιότερα. Και φαίνεται ότι οι πολύ μεγαλύτεροι συγγενείς τους έχουν μερικές δικές τους εκπλήξεις. Οι τζάγκουαρ, για παράδειγμα, θεωρούνταν από καιρό μοναχικά ζώα, με τα αρσενικά και τα θηλυκά γενικά να κρατούν αποστάσεις…
items.descriptionOriginal: Cats have a way of messing with our expectations. Even the humble house cat is proving itself to be less aloof and antisocial than we formerly thought. And it seems their much bigger relatives have a few surprises of their own. Jaguars, for instance, have long been considered solitary animals, with males and females generally keeping their distance except during mating season and when mothers raise their cubs. But after watching jaguars for 13 years, researchers found evidence that these famously independent cats may have a more complicated social life than we realized. The researchers conducted their work in Brazil’s Pantanal, a vast tropical wetland that supports one of the world’s highest jaguar densities. This provided a rare opportunity to observe individual cats repeatedly and see how their relationships developed over time. Welcome to the Jaguar ‘coalition’ Jaguar resting on a tree. Photo credit: Canva The study found that, on occasion, male jaguars formed long-lasting partnerships, patrolling, eating, and resting together. Two of the recorded “coalitions,” as the researchers called them, lasted for more than seven years (beating out many Hollywood marriages). These coalitions are still rare, and the data don’t suggest that jaguars are as close-knit as lions or cheetahs. But it does suggest that jaguar relationships are more intertwined than scientists once believed. The 69 jaguars in the study existed in 13 distinct but connected clusters. Most interacted with only a few others, while certain individuals played key roles in keeping those groups connected. Of the 167 interactions researchers recorded, benign encounters were more common than antagonistic ones. Jaguars were more likely to be seen eating, resting, moving, hunting, or playing together than fighting or displaying aggression toward one another. So why are these solitary cats hanging out? Kinship may help explain some of this behavior. Related animals may be more tolerant of one another when cooperation benefits their shared genetic lineage. View this post on Instagram The researchers also point to a higher concentration of available food and females as factors that could make these interactions more likely. When prey is plentiful, jaguars may have less reason to compete over resources, making it easier for them to tolerate one another. Jaguars aren’t the only big cats giving scientists reason to rethink what “solitary” really means Earlier this year, wild tigers also threw scientists for a loop when drone footage showed one female tiger “babysitting” another female tiger’s cubs. Tigers have just as much of a reputation for keeping their distance as jaguars, but tigresses Goma and Jugini told a very different story. Neither study suggests that big cats have recently evolved to live in lion-style prides. Moreover, they show how long-term observation can add nuance and perhaps even overturn rudimentary ideas about animal behavior. Calling a jaguar “solitary,” for instance, can make its social world sound much simpler than it actually is, especially when researchers have the time and technology to watch what happens when these animals are left to their own devices. Jaguars may still spend much of their lives alone, and tigers certainly aren’t forming neighborhood babysitting circles. Still, both examples show that even famously solitary cats have relationships and behaviors that can be easy to miss. Just like with people, the better we understand animals, the harder it becomes to put them into neat categories. The post Scientists spent 13 years watching jaguars. What they saw challenged a long-held belief. appeared first on Upworthy .
